title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
abstract: Evaluates methods for obtaining calibrated answer confidence from RLHF-tuned language models. It finds that verbalized confidence can be better calibrated than conditional probabilities on several QA benchmarks and frames low confidence as a signal for deferral.

admission.reason: The abstract concerns calibrated answer confidence and possible deferral on QA benchmarks, but the open academic gap is specifically calibration and selective prediction for unconstrained free-form generation. Stronger verified candidates in this set directly study long-form or claim-level free-form outputs, so this narrower QA result would not materially strengthen the remaining gap.

title: Improving reliability of large language models via claim-level self-verification and uncertainty calibration
abstract: Presents CLAIM-CAL, which decomposes generated answers into atomic factual claims, applies multiple self-verification probes, aggregates them into an answer-level risk signal, and calibrates that signal post hoc. It evaluates calibrated confidence together with selective accuracy and coverage rather than relying only on error ranking.

admission.reason: The described capability substantially overlaps the verified claim-level calibration candidate 2608.22483: atomic claim decomposition, self-verification signals, post-hoc calibration, and selective accuracy/coverage. Because this identifier is UNCHECKED and a verified candidate already supplies the same core contribution, it does not justify an additional reading slot.

title: Evaluating Content Selection in Summarization: The Pyramid Method
abstract: Introduces the Pyramid Method for evaluating summary content selection using human-identified content units weighted by how often they appear across reference summaries. It provides a foundational mechanism for measuring coverage of important information, although it does not itself solve source attribution, temporal validity, or open-world completeness.

admission.reason: The project status explicitly states that Pyramid already supplies reference-summary content-unit coverage evidence in the admitted corpus. Reading the same foundational method again would duplicate evidence already established rather than close the remaining omission gap. Its identifier is also UNCHECKED.

title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
abstract: Shows that a language model can generate verbalized probabilities whose reported confidence is empirically calibrated. It also tests calibration under distribution shift and introduces CalibratedMath for evaluating verbalized uncertainty.

admission.reason: The abstract establishes verbalized probability calibration and some distribution-shift testing, but its named evaluation setting is CalibratedMath rather than unconstrained free-form generation. The remaining gap specifically concerns free-form abstractive outputs, and multiple verified candidates here directly test long-form or claim-level generation, so this paper would add less incremental value.

title: Automatically Adaptive Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Develops conformal risk control that automatically adapts to input-dependent difficulty rather than relying solely on a single marginal risk target. The method provides approximate conditional risk control and is relevant to continuously adjusting acceptance policies under heterogeneous or changing inputs.

admission.reason: The abstract addresses input-dependent difficulty and approximate conditional conformal risk control, but it does not show continuing temporal or distributional adaptation. For the open non-stationarity gap, 2106.00170 directly treats sequential unknown distribution shift and 2606.29054 treats adaptation of structured-generation risk control, so this candidate does not materially strengthen the targeted gap.
